scope_justification: A human-made work surface and piece of furniture, built to persist as a standing workstation for writing, computing, and craft work.

A limiter is a human-made audio dynamics processor that reduces the gain of a signal when it exceeds a set threshold, preventing it from exceeding a maximum output level. Built to persist as a hardware unit, plugin, and built-in function of mixing consoles and digital audio workstations.
A signal processing technique that creates a series of regularly spaced amplitude peaks and nulls by superimposing a signal onto a delayed, attenuated copy of itself

A human-made audio processing technique or device that intentionally alters a sound signal in a perceptible way, distinct from the source — built to persist as a category spanning hardware pedals, software plugins, and studio processing chains.

A human-made audio processing technique for creating the perception of spatial position — direction, distance, elevation, and ambient field — through signal processing. Built to persist through immersive audio production, binaural rendering, ambisonic encoding, and spatial audio standards.

A speaker is a device that converts electrical audio signals into audible sound waves for reproduction. It is a human-made construct, designed and manufactured to serve the function of sound reproduction in homes, public address systems, recording studios, and countless other applications.
A human-made rule of statistical inference that maps observed data to an estimate of an unknown quantity, built to persist as the central object and unit of comparison of estimation theory.
a human-made system for listening to audio signals during production, reproduction, or performance, built to persist through hardware and software implementations
human-made audio processing configuration where an effect unit is placed in series within a signal chain, built to persist through studio practice, equipment design, and DAW routing conventions

A human-made support fixture shaped to hold sheet music: a flat, slightly inclined reading surface on a post, manufactured as a standalone accessory and built to persist through repeated performance and practice use.

A human-made mathematical theorem — a stated result with a proof, not a discovered natural object — made to persist as a canonical result in DSP and information theory, taught and relied on in every analog-to-digital design.
Ducking is a human-made audio dynamics technique built to persist as a standard processing method in music production, broadcast, and post-production.

A human-made analytical genus of sociolinguistics: the category of systematic, rule-governed linguistic forms that a speech community distinguishes, built to persist as the discipline's instrument for sorting dialects, idiolects, and their kin by the population or situation that characterizes them.

the human-made practice and techniques for creating reverberation effects in audio — using physical spaces, mechanical devices (reverb tanks, plates, springs), or digital algorithms — as a sound-shaping tool in music and audio production

human-made audio processing technique that increases the dynamic range of a signal by attenuating signals below a threshold relative to those above it, built to persist through studio practice, equipment design, and DAW routing conventions
A human-made practice of blending multiple sound sources into a coherent whole, built to persist via studio conventions, DAW workflows, and engineering training.
A human-made signal-processing concept built to persist as a measurable property describing consistent phase relationships in audio signals.
human-made audio dynamics technique that increases gain for signals below a threshold to expand dynamic range, built to persist through DSP implementations and engineering practice

A human-made conceptual measure of the spread between maximum and minimum usable signal levels in a system, expressed as a ratio or in decibels, built to persist as the standard parameter of audio, RF, and imaging specifications.
A human-made audio analysis metric designed to quantify periodicity in a signal by measuring the prominence of the cepstral peak, persisting in speech and music processing literature and software.
A human-made cognitive construct representing an internal model or representation of a physical space, object, or system that can be mentally manipulated and explored without physical interaction.

An information-theoretic measure for model selection that estimates the relative quality of statistical models for a given dataset by balancing goodness-of-fit against model complexity. Human-made: derived from information theory by Hirotugu Akaike (1974), defined by the formula 2k − 2ln(L), and maintained through statistical practice, software packages, and academic literature across disciplines.

A Kalman filter is a human-made recursive estimation algorithm designed to infer the hidden state of a linear dynamical system from noisy measurements, built to persist as a computational method in engineering and statistics.
Spectral-gate is a human-made audio effect that attenuates frequency components below a threshold in the spectral domain, built to persist as a noise-reduction and creative processing tool.

A human-made mathematical structure that assigns to each element of a domain exactly one element of a codomain, built to persist as the central object of mathematical analysis and computation through set-theoretic formalism, notation, pedagogy, and programming-language constructs.

A human-made signal processing procedure designed and maintained for the sake of audio manipulation — changing the fundamental frequency of a sound while preserving (or deliberately altering) its perceptual timbre and temporal structure. Built to persist in music production, voice conversion, and audio analysis pipelines.

The score function is a human-made derivative functional of statistical inference, defined within Fisher's maximum-likelihood framework as the derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to the parameter, built to persist as the bridge object between likelihood, maximum-likelihood estimation, and Fisher information.

A human-made data visualization that maps the frequency spectrum of a signal across time, enabling diagnosis of transient content, harmonic structure, noise characteristics, and spectral evolution. Built to persist through audio analysis practice, speech processing, sonar, and vibration monitoring toolchains.

An electronic device that combines, routes, and adjusts multiple audio signals through faders, knobs, and switchable paths, built through analog or digital signal-processing circuits, built to persist as a central instrument in live sound, recording studios, and broadcast facilities.
A human-made technique for sound reproduction using two or more independent channels to create spatial perception, built to persist as a standard in music, film, and broadcast audio.

Conditional entropy is a human-made measure of remaining uncertainty in one random variable given knowledge of another. It is the constructed map from information theory that quantifies H(Y|X) = -∑ p(x,y) log p(y|x), extending Shannon entropy to the setting of dependent variables. It persists through the mathematical framework of probability theory and its applications in communications, statistics, and machine learning.

Human-made by construction — no natural object redirects or concentrates hand force for a task until shaped for it — and built to persist because each generation re-manufactures the form to fit the unchanged grip of the hand.

A human-made acoustic measurement model that captures how a listener's head, torso, and pinnae filter sound arriving from different directions, built to persist through HRTF databases and spatial audio rendering pipelines.
a mechanical fastener that attaches objects to a desk edge without drilling, built to persist through manufacturing and consumer use

A human-made mathematical function mapping real numbers to positive reals, defined as the power of the base e, built to persist as the canonical growth function of analysis and computation through mathematical formalism, pedagogy, and numerical libraries.

A de-esser is a human-made audio dynamics processor that reduces sibilant frequencies in a signal, built to persist as hardware units, plugins, and built-in functions of mixing consoles and digital audio workstations.

A class of probability distributions whose density can be written in a canonical factorized form involving natural parameters, a base measure, and a log-partition function. Human-made classification devised by Darmois, Pitman, Koopman, and Fisher to unify families sharing conjugacy, sufficient statistics, and maximum-likelihood tractability.

A human-made audio effect technique: sweeping a bandpass filter's center frequency using an LFO or expression control to produce a vocal-like 'wah' sound. Built to persist as a standard effect in guitar pedals, DSP code, and studio processing.
A human-made method of moving through and orienting within a physical or virtual space, using internal cognitive maps or external reference systems.

Pearson's chi-squared statistic is a human-made goodness-of-fit functional, constructed in 1900 by Karl Pearson to compare observed category counts against expected counts, and it is built to persist as the standard form of the chi-squared hypothesis test used throughout statistics.

A human-made hardware/software bridge that converts analog audio signals to digital data and vice versa for recording and playback, built to persist through manufacturing, standards, and computer audio ecosystems.
test

A human-made probability distribution over future or unobserved data, marginalized over the posterior distribution of model parameters. It is the canonical Bayesian tool for out-of-sample prediction, built to persist as the standard probabilistic forecast in Bayesian analysis.

A human-made element of musical notation: a set of parallel horizontal lines (standardly five) whose lines and spaces form the reference frame for placing written pitches, built to persist as the standardized frame of written music across engraving, typesetting, and pedagogy.

A human-made mathematical representation of a physical or abstract system as a set of first-order differential or difference equations relating state variables, inputs, and outputs, built to persist as the standard formalism for modeling dynamic systems in engineering and control theory.

Power divergence is a family of statistical divergences parameterized by α, including both Rényi and Tsallis divergences as special cases. It is a human-authored mathematical framework for measuring the discrepancy between probability distributions, used in statistics, information theory, and machine learning.

A saturator is a human-made audio effects processor — either hardware unit or software plugin — designed to add controlled harmonic saturation and gentle distortion to audio signals by driving analog-style circuits, transformer models, or tube emulation into nonlinear operation. Built to persist as a dedicated processing stage in mixing chains.

The human-made family of audio techniques that modify a signal's dynamic range by level-dependent variable gain (compression, limiting, expansion, gating), built to persist as the shared parameter set and vocabulary of studio and live-sound engineering practice.
Gain-staging is a human-made audio engineering practice built to persist as a standard method for maintaining optimal signal levels throughout a processing chain.
Human-made audio effect technique built to persist as a reusable DSP method for creating moving spectral notches via frequency-domain delay modulation.
A human-made element of musical notation: a glyph that fixes a duration of silence on the staff, built to persist as the counterpart of the note — the atomic unit of written silence.

An electronic device designed specifically to amplify audio signals to levels suitable for driving headphones, built through purpose-designed circuits with high output impedance management and voltage swing capability, built to persist through portable and studio audio equipment.

A human-made mathematical concept in information theory and statistics: a measure of how one probability distribution diverges from a reference distribution. Built to persist in information theory, machine learning, Bayesian inference, and large deviation theory.
A human-made restoration stage built to persist as the standard level-recovery element of every dynamic-range compressor.
human-made audio processing technique that intentionally clips or saturates an electronic signal to add harmonic content and create a gritty, compressed sound character
human-made audio processing configuration where an effect unit is fed via a parallel split and mixed back, built to persist through studio practice, equipment design, and DAW routing conventions
A human-made standing-height work surface for craft work, built to persist as a workshop fixture that holds material and tools for hand-tool shaping.

A human-made family of statistical divergences parameterized by a convex function f, built to persist as a unifying framework in information theory that includes KL-divergence, Hellinger distance, and χ²-divergence as special cases.

A human-made timing construct of digital audio: the periodic pulse train that stamps every sample with its position, built to persist as the master grid every digital recorder, interface, and player must agree on.

A preamp (preamplifier) is a human-made electronic circuit that amplifies weak electrical signals to a usable level before further processing or power amplification. Built to persist as a fundamental stage in audio chains, microphone circuits, guitar effects, and measurement systems.

A dynamic range compression device or algorithm that reduces the amplitude of signals exceeding a threshold, controlled by attack time, release time, ratio, and threshold parameters. Human-made as an audio processing tool built into hardware units, software plugins, and broadcast equipment, designed to persist as a standard component of signal chains.

A human-made audio effect and technique that produces a slow, periodic variation in the pitch of a sound signal by summing a low-frequency oscillator into the pitch of the source, creating a wavering or throbbing quality — built to persist as a standard effect in synthesizers, guitar and vocal processors, and studio plugins, controlled by rate (LFO frequency, conventionally 4-8 Hz) and depth (pitch deviation in cents).

A wah-pedal is a human-made guitar effects device that sweeps a filter's center frequency via a foot-operated control (typically a potentiometer), producing a vocal-like tonal shift. Built to persist as a hardware pedal design, a signal-processing concept, and a guitar technique taught across generations of players.

A human-made mathematical bound designed to provide a tractable lower bound on the log marginal likelihood (evidence) in Bayesian models with latent variables, built to persist as the optimization objective in variational inference and the theoretical foundation of variational autoencoders.

A human-made electronic device or circuit designed to increase the amplitude of an electrical signal while preserving its waveform characteristics — built to persist as the foundational building block of audio systems, radio equipment, measurement instruments, and guitar pedals.

A human-made optimization method in machine learning that preconditions gradient descent using the Fisher information metric, persisting as a standard technique for training models with parameter-space geometry.

A human-made audio processing technique: duplicating a signal, applying slight pitch variation and time delay to each copy, and mixing the copies back with the original to thicken the perceived sound — built to persist as a standard effect in guitar pedals, synthesizers, and studio processing.

A human-made statistical measure in Bayesian inference that quantifies the strength of evidence provided by observed data in favor of one hypothesis or model over another. Built to persist in Bayesian model comparison, hypothesis testing, and evidence-based decision theory.

A human-made window function — the named triangular taper applied to a finite data segment before Fourier analysis to trade main-lobe width against spectral-leakage reduction, persisting as a standardized formula in signal-processing textbooks and DSP toolkits.

A human-made probability distribution over the parameter space of a statistical model, encoding beliefs before data is observed. It is a formal component of Bayesian inference, built to persist as the subjective starting point of all Bayesian analysis.
A human-made framework of methods for analyzing and transforming signals across any representation domain, built to persist through engineering practice, software libraries, and academic curricula.

The second central moment of a random variable, quantifying the expected squared deviation of outcomes from their mean — a human-made mathematical construct for measuring dispersion in probability distributions.
A human-made mechanical audio delay mechanism using a continuous magnetic tape loop driven by capstans, built to persist as a studio effect and hardware component.

a signal processing technique where the amplitude of a carrier signal is varied by a modulating signal, producing sum and difference frequency components, used in communications, audio synthesis, and signal processing

A synthesizer is a human-made electronic instrument built to generate and shape sound through electronic oscillators, filters, and modulation circuits. It is designed to produce musical tones from nothing, unlike instruments that only amplify or modify naturally occurring vibrations. Its persistence depends on electrical power (or battery) and user configuration of its parameters.

A human-made mathematical quantity representing the logarithm of the likelihood function, serving as the foundation for parameter estimation, model selection, and statistical inference across scientific disciplines.
A human-made optimal linear filter — a noise-removal and estimation standard built to persist in signal processing, defined by the minimum mean-squared error criterion between estimate and target.

Human-made: a purpose-built device whose very function is transforming a signal or quantity across representational domains, persisting as a physical or software artifact with a reproducible transfer law.

A human-made window function — the three-term cosine-sum taper with a first side lobe near -58 dB, persisting as a standard formula in signal-processing textbooks and DSP toolkits where side-lobe suppression outweighs main-lobe broadening.
a human-made signal reconstruction technique built to persist in audio processing practice and software libraries

A human-made mathematical quantity in statistical inference that measures how much information an observable random variable or sample carries about an unknown parameter governing its distribution, constructed to persist as a core measure of estimation accuracy in mathematical statistics.

A human-made engineering technique: it exists because humans designed circuits to scale weak signals with external power, and it persists as circuit topologies, gain and level specifications in datasheets and standards, and the repeated design practice of every preamplifier, power amplifier, and mixing stage.

Spectral processing is a human-made method of analyzing and manipulating the frequency-domain representation of a signal, using mathematical transforms (notably the Fourier transform) to decompose time-domain waveforms into their constituent frequency components. It persists through algorithmic implementation in DSP libraries, software tools (FFT analyzers, spectral editors), and engineering education.
Mid-side processing is a human-made audio technique created to manipulate stereo image via mid and side channels, persisting through studio practice and plugin implementations.

A human-made family of entropy measures parameterized by order α, introduced by Rényi (1961), that generalizes Shannon entropy by trading sensitivity to rare events (low α) against sensitivity to dominant events (high α). Built to persist as a standard tool in information theory, cryptography, and statistical physics.
A human-made mathematical quantity extending Shannon entropy to continuous probability distributions, persisting as a core concept in information theory, statistics, and machine learning.

A conceptual framework in cognitive psychology describing how prior exposure to a stimulus unconsciously influences responses to a subsequent stimulus, without conscious awareness or intentional effort.

A human-made mathematical framework that specifies a family of probability distributions parameterized by unknown quantities, built to persist as the foundational object of statistical inference, estimation, and hypothesis testing.
A clipper is a human-made audio dynamics processor designed to hard-limit peaks by clipping the waveform, built to persist as hardware units and software plugins in mixing chains.
A human-made signal-analysis block built to persist as the standard level-detection primitive inside dynamic audio processing.

A transducer is a device or system that converts energy from one form to another, enabling measurement, control, or communication. It is human-made through design and manufacturing, existing as a class of engineered devices spanning electro-acoustic, electromechanical, thermal, and optical domains.

A human-made named interval of Western music — the smallest step of the chromatic scale, in its diatonic and chromatic qualities — built to persist through interval nomenclature, staff notation, and keyboard and fret layout.
Bit-crusher is a human-made audio effect that degrades digital audio by reducing bit depth and sample rate, built to persist as a studio effect and plugin.
human-made audio signal processing device or algorithm that adjusts the amplitude of specific frequency bands within an audio signal, enabling tonal shaping and spectral balancing

Gain is the human-made conceptual measure of amplification ratio — the quantitative relationship between output and input signal levels, expressed as a dimensionless ratio or in decibels. Built to persist as a standard parameter across audio engineering, RF design, and control systems.

A human-made family of statistical divergences between probability distributions, parameterized by the order α, introduced by Rényi (1961) and built to persist as a standard named family in information theory and statistical inference.

A human-made filter design standard — the classic maximally-flat magnitude-response prototype — built to persist as the reference filter family in signal-processing textbooks and design toolkits, from which analog and digital IIR filters are derived.

A human-made technique and circuit for capturing the instantaneous value of a continuous-time signal and maintaining that value for a defined period; built to persist through sampling systems, data-acquisition hardware, and analog-to-digital conversion.

A human-made mathematical function derived from a statistical model that evaluates how well each parameter value explains observed data, built to persist as the foundational object of frequentist statistical inference and maximum-likelihood estimation.

A human-made audio effect device that produces echoes by recording a signal onto a moving magnetic tape loop and playing it back after a mechanical delay, built to persist as a studio effect and vintage hardware.

A statistical model for binary outcome data that uses the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution as its link function, built for parameter estimation and hypothesis testing in regression contexts.

A human-made iterative optimization algorithm designed to find maximum-likelihood estimates in statistical models with latent variables, built to persist as a standard procedure in statistics, machine learning, and computational linguistics.

A human-made nonlinear signal-processing method that generates harmonics by applying an amplitude transfer function to a signal, built to persist as a digital algorithm in audio plugins, DSP chips, and software synthesizers.
Sidechain is a human-made audio routing technique built to persist as a standard method in mixing, dynamics processing, and broadcast.
Human-made objective metric for speech quality assessment, built to persist in audio engineering literature and evaluation pipelines.

A human-made feedback control circuit that locks the phase and frequency of an internally generated signal to a reference signal, built to persist as the standard block of frequency synthesis, clock recovery, and sample-clock generation in communications and audio hardware.

A normative legal threshold invented in common-law practice to protect the accused, built to persist through statute, constitutional amendment, and the standard jury instructions that recite it verbatim.

A human-made concept mapping the natural phenomenon of encoding information in media external to the mind — artifacts, symbols, or structures carrying informational content independently of any specific holder. Built to persist through the study of communication, cognition, and information design.

A comparator is a human-made electronic circuit or system that compares two input signals and produces an output indicating their relationship — whether one exceeds the other, they are equal, or which is larger. Built to persist as a building block of audio dynamics processing, control systems, measurement instruments, and logic design.

A human-made element of musical notation: a glyph (sharp, flat, or natural) that modifies the pitch of a note, built to persist as part of the standard Western notation system through shared convention and teaching.
Variational inference is a human-made approximation method for Bayesian posterior distributions, built to persist as a computational algorithm in machine learning and statistics.

Clipping is the human-made concept describing waveform distortion that occurs when a signal exceeds the maximum amplitude capacity of a system, causing the peaks to be truncated or 'clipped.' Built to persist as a diagnostic and design concept in audio engineering, RF, and digital signal processing.

The human-made probability of the observed data under a model with its parameters integrated out, built to persist as the normalizing constant of Bayes's theorem, the numerator of the Bayes factor, and the quantity whose decomposition drives variational inference.
A human-made measurement device and software instrument built to persist through studio standards, hardware implementations, and DAW plugins for monitoring audio dynamics.

A low-frequency oscillator is an electronic or algorithmic signal source that generates periodic waveforms at frequencies below the audible range (typically 0.01-20 Hz), used to modulate parameters in synthesis, effects, and control systems.
a small accessory designed to hold headphones when not in use, built to persist through manufacturing and consumer use

A human-made signal-processing technique: the operating principle by which FM radio broadcasting, two-way radio, and FM synthesis modulate a carrier, built to persist as a mathematical relation and as engineered oscillator hardware and software.

A signal-chain is a human-made conceptual model in audio engineering that describes the ordered sequence of processing stages through which an audio signal passes, persisting through notation, teaching, and studio practice.

A human-made linguistic category for words and phrases that belong to informal everyday speech rather than formal or technical registers, created through social usage patterns and sustained by community communication practices.

A human-made second-order filter section built to persist as the fundamental building block of IIR filter implementation in DSP systems, defined by its two poles and two zeros and parameterized by five coefficients per section.

A human-made family of statistical divergences parameterized by the order q, introduced by Tsallis (1988) in non-extensive statistical mechanics and built to persist as a standard named family in information theory, information geometry, and machine learning, where the q-parameter tunes sensitivity to outliers.
human-made audio dynamics technique that blends compressed and uncompressed signals to preserve transients while increasing perceived loudness

A speaker dedicated to reproducing low frequencies, human-made through purpose-built drivers and enclosures that radiate into a room, built to persist through home-theater, studio, and live-sound practice where it operates as a dedicated low end beneath a crossover point.
A human-made audio analysis metric designed to quantify spectral shape and persist in DSP literature and software.

human-made audio signal routing technique that splits an audio signal into two or more frequency bands for separate processing or amplification, built to persist through studio practice, speaker design, and live sound engineering
A human-made family of statistical scoring rules that trade goodness-of-fit against model complexity, built to persist as the standard comparison yardstick of model-selection practice.

A human-made audio effect technique: mixing a signal with a phase-shifted version created by all-pass filter cascades to produce a sweeping comb-filter 'swoosh.' Built to persist as a standard effect in guitar pedals, DSP code, and studio processing.
a signal processing device or algorithm that multiplies two input signals together to produce sum and difference frequencies, used as a timbral effect in music and audio synthesis

A human-made kind of document: a printed, engraved, or digitally rendered artifact bearing a musical score in standard notation, produced for a performing reader and built to persist as a product category across performance and practice use.

A delay-line is a signal storage construct that records an input and releases it after a controlled time offset, implemented in hardware as tapped transmission lines or analog delay elements, and in software as circular buffers or queue-based FIFO structures in DSP systems.
A human-made audio processing device or algorithm that changes the pitch of an audio signal while preserving its duration, built to persist as hardware pedal, rack unit, or software plugin.
A human-made speech synthesis technique built to persist as a compact parametric representation of voice for telecommunications and musical experimentation.

A human-made control architecture in which a system's output is measured and compared to a desired reference, with the error signal used to drive corrective adjustment; built to persist through engineering practice from mechanical governors to modern digital controllers.

A smooth approximation to the maximum function: log-sum-exp(x) = log(∑_i exp(x_i)). Human-made computational construct used in optimization, machine learning, and probability to replace the non-differentiable max with a differentiable surrogate, and in numerically stable computation of log-probabilities via the log-sum-exp trick.
A human-made audio effect technique that models the non-linear distortion and compression characteristics of magnetic tape recording, built to persist as a plugin/algorithm and hardware emulation.

Headroom is the human-made concept describing the difference between the maximum operating level of an audio system and its normal operating level, expressed in decibels. Built to persist as a design and operational parameter in audio engineering, ensuring signals can transiently exceed nominal levels without distortion.

A human-made statistical function — the probability of fixed observed data re-read as a function of the unknown parameter — built to persist as the central object of estimation theory, maximum-likelihood estimation, and Bayesian updating.

A human-made formal structure of category theory — a quadruple of objects, morphisms, composition, and identities — built with axioms so that structure-preserving maps between mathematical domains can be compared, persisting as the ambient parameter of every morphism in the standard formalization of category theory.

A human-made probability distribution over model parameters after observing data, computed by applying Bayes rule to combine the prior distribution with the likelihood. It is the central object of Bayesian inference, built to persist as the posterior belief state in all Bayesian analysis.
A human-made audio processing device designed to persist as a circuit and software implementation that adds upper harmonics to a sound source.

An electronic circuit or integrated chip that reconstructs a continuous analog voltage waveform from a stream of discrete digital codes, human-made through precision analog design and silicon fabrication, built to persist as the standard bridge between digital sources and analog amplification in audio, video, and control practice.
A human-made electroacoustic listening device — a pair of drivers worn at the ears — built to persist through mass manufacture, interface standardization, and consumer replacement cycles.

Overdrive is a human-made audio effect: the deliberate soft-clipping of an electrical audio signal by pushing an amplifier or circuit beyond its linear operating range, producing warm harmonic saturation. Built to persist as a circuit design, pedal implementation, and sonic technique taught across guitar and recording practice.

A human-made mathematical identity that splits the expected prediction error of a statistical estimator into bias squared, variance, and irreducible error, persisting in machine learning theory and teaching.

A human-made family of functions in probability theory and information theory that quantify the difference between two probability distributions, built to persist as a mathematical framework for comparing statistical models.

A human-made map of processing operations performed on audio signals: amplification, filtering, mixing, effects, spatialization, and analysis. Built to persist through audio engineering practice, DAW software, studio education, and hardware toolchains. Distinguished from general signal-processing by its focus on audible-range (20 Hz–20 kHz) acoustic signals and perceptual criteria.

A human-made system and practice for directing audio signals between sources and destinations within an audio system, built to persist through implementation in hardware mixers, software DAWs, and patch bays

A human-made element of musical notation: a glyph (notehead with optional stem, flags, or beams) that fixes one pitch and one duration on the staff, built to persist as the atomic unit of written music across engraving, typesetting, and pedagogy.

A human-made signal-processing technique family that analyzes audio into compact parameters and resynthesizes from them — built to persist because it is how speech coders, formant vocoders, and DAW effects encode and transform the voice.
A class of causal digital and analog filters designed by humans to minimize phase delay for a given magnitude response, persisting in engineering practice and signal-processing literature.

A sampler is a human-made electronic musical instrument built to record, store, and playback audio fragments (samples) triggered by performance input. It is designed to reuse previously captured sounds as playable material, extending the range of available timbres beyond what acoustic instruments or synthesizers can produce. Its persistence depends on digital storage and a playback engine.

A human-made map of digital audio's temporal resolution parameter: the number of discrete samples taken per second to convert an analog audio signal into digital form. Built to persist as a specification governing fidelity, frequency response (via the Nyquist limit), and system compatibility in all digital audio workflows. The map defines discrete values (8kHz through 384kHz) and their acoustic consequences.

A statistical technique that combines predictions from multiple candidate models using weighted averaging, reducing selection uncertainty and improving predictive accuracy compared to single-model selection. Human-made: formalized by Burnham and Anderson (2002), defined by the weighted-sum formula, maintained through statistical practice and software across disciplines.

A human-made audio effect that periodically varies the amplitude of a sound signal to produce a pulsating or quavering sound, controlled by rate (LFO frequency) and depth — built to persist as a standard effect in guitar amplifiers, stompbox pedals, synthesizers, and studio processing.
A hardware device that converts continuous analog signals into discrete digital data for recording, processing, and transmission in digital systems, using sampling and quantization.

A human-made formal object of category theory — an arrow between objects in a category — built with composition and identity axioms so it can serve as the universal language of structure-preserving maps. It persists as the foundational vocabulary of category theory across mathematics and computer science.

A human-made audio effect technique — the discrete repeat of a signal via stored-delay retrieval with feedback — built to persist as a standard effect in guitar pedals, studio DSP, and synthesizer patches.

A human-made mathematical framework that applies differential geometry to spaces of probability distributions, treating families of distributions as manifolds equipped with a Fisher information metric, persisting in statistics, machine learning, and information theory as the geometric study of statistical inference.

A human-made statistical inference method designed to find the parameter values that maximize the probability (or likelihood) of observed data under a specified model, built to persist as the standard parameter-estimation procedure in frequentist statistics and machine learning.
Audio bus is a human-made audio routing construct built to persist as a channel for collective processing and mixing in studio practice.

A human-made support fixture: a manufactured base-and-arm structure that holds an object (headphones, a lamp, sheet music, a tool) upright at a chosen position when it is not in active use — made-side because it is produced as a fixture and built to persist across repeated use of the held object.

A human-made element of Western musical notation: a glyph (an arc enclosing a dot) placed over a note, chord, or rest that suspends its rhythm, built to persist as part of the standard notation system through shared performance convention, engraving and typesetting practice, and teaching.

A human-made element of musical notation: a vertical boundary mark on the staff that delimits bars, built to persist as part of the standard Western notation system through shared convention, engraving and typesetting practice, and teaching.

A human-made named interval of Western music: the pitch distance between two tones whose frequencies stand in a 2:1 ratio, built to persist as the fixed unit of transposition, register, and pitch-class identity through tuning standards, harmonic theory, and notation.

A human-made tuning system — the convention dividing the octave into twelve equal semitones — built to persist as the dominant interval framework of Western music through instrument manufacture, international pitch standards, and notation.

A human-made learning algorithm used to approximate maximum-likelihood training for Boltzmann machines by contrasting data distribution with model distribution, persisting through machine learning practice and computational implementations.

A human-made tonal framework — an organized set of pitches and their hierarchical functional relations centered on a tonic — built to persist through key signatures in staff notation, the circle of fifths, harmony pedagogy, and the naming practice of composition and performance.

A legal principle in adversarial justice systems that places the burden of proof on the prosecution and requires proof beyond reasonable doubt before conviction, built to persist as a procedural safeguard against wrongful deprivation of liberty.
A human-made signal-processing technique built to persist as a class of speech enhancement algorithms that estimate time-frequency masks to separate speech from noise.
human-made audio signal processing device or algorithm that attenuates or mutes a signal when its level falls below a set threshold, used to reduce unwanted background noise between sound events

A human-made information-theoretic measure that assigns to each event in a probability space the amount of information or surprisal conveyed by that event, computed as the negative logarithm of its probability, persisting in communication theory, statistics, and machine learning as a fundamental building block for entropy, divergence, and mutual information.

A human-made audio processing technique that creates spatial sound perception using two independent audio channels to simulate three-dimensional auditory space. Built to persist through headphone-based audio production, virtual reality audio, gaming, and music production. Distinguished from ambisonics by scope: binaural rendering uses head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) for personalized spatial cues, while ambisonics encodes a full spherical sound field for multi-channel or headphone playback.

A human-made record object in version-control systems, built to persist as the immutable unit of history: each commit snapshots a project's state with attribution and message, and it persists because it is hash-addressed, linked into a history graph, and propagated through clones and pushes.
A human-made audio signal processing algorithm built to persist as a phase-coherent variant of the phase vocoder used in time-stretching and pitch-shifting.

A human-made signal processing technique for efficient convolution by discarding overlap regions, built to persist in DSP literature and implementations.

A human-made specification of the smallest distinguishable interval in a time-domain measurement or display system, defined by the sampling rate, frame rate, or refresh rate of the apparatus.

Chi-squared divergence is a human-made measure of difference between two probability distributions, defined as D_χ²(P||Q) = ∫ (p(x) - q(x))² / q(x) dx. It is the f-divergence generated by φ(t) = (t-1)² and serves as a computationally convenient alternative to KL-divergence in goodness-of-fit testing and density estimation. It persists through its role in mathematical statistics and hypothesis testing.
